Subject: FintechCo API auth & key management - post-demo

Hi Alex + Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps around API authentication/key management based on what we heard from your security and infra teams: 

Summary:
- Goal: Production integration that meets FintechCo security posture (short-lived creds, rotation, auditable key usage) while keeping developer experience simple for your product teams.
- Primary options we discussed: scoped API keys (easy), service accounts with JWT exchange (recommended for server-to-server), OAuth (if you need user-level delegated access).

Notes from the demo / items we think matter:
- You want per-environment keys (dev/prod) + the ability to rotate keys without rollout downtime.
- Need audit logs for key usage and ability to revoke quickly.
- Embeddings/reranker calls should be scoped so they cannot use data-exfiltration endpoints (we can enforce per-key route policies).

What Redwood provides today (high level):
- Scoped API keys: labelable, environment-scoped, and route-restricted.
- Service accounts: long-lived credentials that exchange for short-lived JWTs (recommended for backend services).
- Rotation: support for key rotation with staged rollouts and optional prefix-based routing to allow zero-downtime rotations.
- SDK support: token refresh helpers + sample code for automated rotation.
- Audit & compliance: token-level usage logs available in Console; SOC2 docs available on request.

Attachments: redwood-auth-patterns.pdf (patterns + recommended flows), integration-checklist.xlsx (action items + personas).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which auth approach you want to pursue for the initial POC (scoped API keys vs service accounts).
2) If service accounts, schedule a 60-minute deep-tech call (Dev + Marcus from our infra team) to go over JWT exchange, KMS/HSM integrations, and rotation cadence.
3) We’ll provide a POC sandbox org with sample keys and an initial set of route policies for you to test.

Can you confirm preferred auth approach and send a couple of times for next week if you want the deep-tech call?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: integration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks Marissa — super helpful rundown. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock the approach: 

1) For service accounts + JWT exchange, what TTL do you recommend for the short-lived tokens? We want tight windows (minutes) for high privilege calls but not so short that it negatively impacts throughput for embeddings calls.
2) Does Redwood SDK support automatic rotation and swap of keys without changing client wiring? Our ops team prefers a model where they can rotate keys in KMS and have clients pick up the new key transparently.
3) Can you scope keys by capability (e.g., embeddings-only, reranker-only, generate-only)? We want to separate allowed operations per key.

Also, would love to see a sample of the JWT exchange flow and any sample code you have for token refresh — can your team drop the sample code in the sandbox?

— Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, FintechCo

Alex — great questions. Looping in Dev (SDK) and Marcus (infra) to answer the specifics; below is a concise summary + what we’ll include in the sandbox: 

Answers (short):
- TTL: For backend service accounts we recommend short-lived tokens in the ~15–60 minute range. For high-volume embedder workers you can use a slightly longer TTL (2–4 hours) coupled with request signing to reduce refresh churn.
- SDK rotation: Redwood SDKs include a token provider interface. If you store a primary key in your KMS and perform rotation via the Console or API, the SDK token provider can automatically pickup the new signing key when you run the rotation script — no client code change needed if you use the recommended token provider pattern. We’ll add an example script to the sandbox.
- Capability scoping: Yes — keys can be scoped at the route level and by capability (embeddings, rerank, generate). We also support ACL-style labels so ops can enforce per-team policies.

What we’ll drop in the sandbox:
- Sample JWT exchange flow (service-account-key -> short-lived JWT -> exchange for access token).
- Example SDK token provider (Node + Python) with KMS rotation hooks.
- A set of route policies that illustrate embeddings-only and reranker-only keys.

Dev + Marcus, can you add the sample code and the token sample file to the sandbox org by EOD Monday? Alex/Priya — if you confirm the approach we’ll provision the sandbox and a short-lived set of keys for testing.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alex / Priha — Neha from Security at Redwood here. Thanks for flagging SOC2 and rotation details. Short answers: 

- SOC2: I’ll share our SOC2 summary report and mapping document to common controls. Expect a secure link to the SOC2 artifact and a short control mapping by EOD Monday.
- Rotation policy: Redwood supports KMS-backed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and recommends a 90-day rotation for root/service account keys with automatic rotation of short-lived tokens (<= 60 minutes) for service-to-service flows. We keep token-level usage logs for 365 days in the Console (can be exported to your SIEM).

Marissa / Dev — I’ll add the SOC2 link and a one-page key rotation statement to the sandbox folder.
